AUTHOR: Pengying
TITLE: Underwater Fish Classification of Trout and Grayling
VENUE: 2019 15th International Conference on Signal-Image Technology & Internet-Based Systems (SITIS)
SPECIES: brown trout (Salmo trutta), European grayling (Thymallus thymallus)
DATA: NINA sensor-triggered underwater videos from fish ladder (own partner data)
V_EV: [V1 recoded NR on verification: statement not about the study's own water clarity] Sec. III.A: 'the videos have varying light conditions (as they as taken during both day and night), many bubbles ... low sharpness and low contrast.'
D2: 80/20 random per class (7376 train / 1844 test frames)
D_EV: Sec. III.A: 'Eighty percent of each class are chosen randomly to be a training set and the remaining are test set'
R_EV: Sec. III.C: 'the networks with high accuracy will be tested with the incomplete images' (same NINA dataset, partial-fish frames)
C_EV: Sec. III.B: AlexNet last layer 'modified ... from 1000 to 2 classes: grayling and trout' - argmax classification, no threshold reported
E_EV: Sec. III.D: 'The accuracy is computed by dividing the correct classification output by all test set.' Only accuracy/F1 reported.
METR: Accuracy, precision, recall, F1, confusion matrix
NOTE: Every frame of ~1-min videos extracted; random frame split implies strong near-duplicate leakage (not discussed). Incomplete-fish test set (3900 frames) from same videos, not external. PRE inferred from 1000-class AlexNet head (ImageNet not named explicitly). Fig.1 caption mentions fish at different distances qualitatively; no range reported.
